Additionally, `common/src/util/stats.ts` provides dependency-free statistical helpers including Wilson intervals, Newcombe's difference test, and chi-square sample-ratio-mismatch checks for experiment readouts. ai.title: Freestyle VM sandbox and terminal upstream guard for BuffBench
ai.summary: A new `--freestyle` flag lets BuffBench run each agent task in its own isolated Freestyle VM, which polls for completion and powers off automatically to prevent local sleep from tainting results. This mechanism ships the bench code and necessary environment variables to the VM while excluding eval answer files. ai.title: Classify Bun compressed stream cuts as transient network errors
ai.summary: The shared error classification in `common` now treats `ZlibError` and `BrotliDecompressionError` as transient network failures, enabling the SDK's retry logic to recover from dropped connections during compressed SSE transfers. This change addresses a failure mode where Bun's fetch throws a `ZlibError` when a gzip-compressed response body is terminated before the compressed stream finishes, such as when a web deploy scales down an instance and closes the HTTP connection. Previously, these errors were not recognized as transient, causing the agent to fail the turn instead of retrying, which resulted in hundreds of failed requests during deploys after SSE gzip compression was enabled at 100%.

entries.summary: New files: `common/src/util/code-search-flags.ts`.

acceptedPr.title: Cache existing hidden directories in codeSearch to avoid redundant stat calls
acceptedPr.author: nordicnode
acceptedPr.body:
## Summary

- In `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts`, de-duplicate repeated `fs.statSync` inspections for blessed hidden directories (`.agents`, `.claude`, `.github`, `.gitlab`, `.circleci`, `.husky`) using a bounded in-memory cache with a 1-second burst TTL.
- **1-second burst TTL**: Scoped specifically to rapid bursts of queries (e.g. concurrent tool calls or tight sequential searches within the same agent turn). A short 1s window guarantees that any cross-turn actions (such as scaffolding `.github/` or `.husky/` during project setup) naturally see fresh filesystem state.
- **O(1) LRU eviction**: Bounded to `MAX_CACHE_SIZE = 100` directories. On cache hit or insertion, entry recency is refreshed in `Map`; when full, the least-recently-used entry is evicted rather than clearing the whole cache.
- **Targeted invalidation**: `clearHiddenDirsCache(dir?)` supports invalidating a specific directory or clearing all entries.
- **Realistic framing**: Acknowledges that `fs.statSync` on 6 paths in OS cache is sub-millisecond and ripgrep process execution dominates overall search latency. This change acts as a lightweight burst de-duplication to eliminate redundant disk checks and ENOENT exceptions during rapid searches within the same directory root.
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Replaced static comparisons with dynamic filesystem tests in `sdk/src/__tests__/code-search.test.ts` verifying:
  - Cache shielding within TTL window.
  - Immediate discovery when a directory is created and `clearHiddenDirsCache` is called.
  - Immediate discovery when a directory is removed and `clearHiddenDirsCache` is called.
  - Automatic directory discovery upon 1-second TTL expiration without manual cache clearing.
  - Targeted cache clearing on specific directories.
  - Proper LRU eviction of oldest entries when cache capacity is exceeded.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test src/__tests__/code-search.test.ts` (37 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] `bun run --cwd sdk test` (542 passed, 0 failed across 41 files)
- [x] `bun run --cwd sdk typecheck` (0 errors)
- [x] `bun run build:sdk` (successful build)
- [x] `bun freebuff/cli/build.ts 0.0.0-ci` (successful binary build)
- [x] Binary smoke test: `bun cli/scripts/smoke-binary.ts cli/bin/freebuff` (OK)
- [x] Prettier check: `bun x prettier --check sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts sdk/src/__tests__/code-search.test.ts` (All matched files use Prettier code style)

ai.title: Refuse exec-capable ripgrep flags in code search
ai.summary: The SDK code search tool now refuses ripgrep flags that execute external commands, including `--pre`, `--pre-glob`, `--hostname-bin`, `--search-zip`, and the short form `-z`, to prevent model-generated searches from running arbitrary programs without a terminal tool. The shared utility `codeSearchExecFlagRefusal` in `common` scans every parsed flag token and returns an error message naming the specific refused flag before any process spawn. Separately, the `write_file` tool documentation in `common` was updated to clarify that local hosts accept absolute paths that are not limited to the project root.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/util/code-search-flags.ts` defines `codeSearchExecFlagRefusal` which checks against `RIPGREP_EXEC_LONG_FLAGS` and `RIPGREP_EXEC_SHORT_FLAGS`; `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts` imports this function and calls it on `flagsArray` before spawning ripgrep. Additionally, `common/src/tools/params/tool/write-file.ts` updates the `path` description to mention absolute path support for local hosts.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the refusal message is surfaced to the user in the CLI UI or only returned to the model as a tool error.

changes.what: Code search now rejects ripgrep flags that spawn external programs via a new shared refusal check.
New utility module defines the set of executable ripgrep flags and the token-scanning function to detect them.
The write_file tool parameter documentation and Zod schema description now state that local hosts accept absolute paths outside the project.

ai.summary: New `csvCell` and `csvRow` functions in `common/src/util/csv.ts` implement RFC 4180-compliant CSV field serialization with formula-injection protection. Values matching `FORMULA_PREFIX` (leading Unicode whitespace followed by `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@`) are prefixed with a literal apostrophe so spreadsheet applications treat them as text. The implementation quotes fields containing double quotes, commas, or newlines, doubling any embedded quotes.
ai.evidence: The commit adds a new file `common/src/util/csv.ts` defining `csvCell` and `csvRow` utilities, with `FORMULA_PREFIX` regex to detect and escape formula-injection characters (like `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) by prefixing an apostrophe.
ai.unknowns: The immediate consumer of these new CSV utilities is not visible in this commit; they are in place but not yet wired into any existing export or report generation.

eli5.text: The team added new rules to keep spreadsheets from running dangerous commands when opening data exported by the service. This change is internal and does not affect how you use the assistant today. It is in place now, but no existing export or report feature uses these new rules yet, so there is no visible effect or action needed for you.

entries.summary: New files: `common/src/util/log-redaction.ts`.

ai.title: Add log redaction and agent output token ceiling
ai.summary: A new utility module in `common` redacts URLs, request bodies, and headers in error logs to prevent sensitive data like prompts and API keys from leaking into telemetry sinks like PostHog and Axiom. This change also introduces a `maxOutputTokens` ceiling to agent definitions, enforced in the agent runtime so that a caller can lower, but never raise, the limit set by the agent template. Additionally, a new analytics event for freebuff title rate limiting is registered in the shared constants.
ai.evidence: The new file `common/src/util/log-redaction.ts` defines `redactUrlForLog`, `summarizeRequestBodyForLog`, and `redactHeadersForLog` to strip query parameters, request bodies, and sensitive headers before logs reach PostHog or Axiom. The diff also adds `maxOutputTokens` to `AgentDefinition` in `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts` and implements a ceiling-enforcement logic in `packages/agent-runtime/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts` using `Math.min` between caller and template limits.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not specify which existing telemetry consumers are updated to utilize the new `maxOutputTokens` field in agent templates outside of the runtime stream.

changes.what: Adds a log-redaction module that strips URL queries, summarizes LLM request bodies into shape-only metadata, and masks sensitive headers.
Integrates the redaction logic into the shared error and log-data serializers to protect telemetry payloads.
Updates the API client's network error formatter to redact URL query parameters before they reach the user or telemetry.
Introduces `maxOutputTokens` as a ceiling in agent definitions and enforces it in the prompt stream by taking the minimum of the caller and template values.
Registers a new `FREEBUFF_TITLE_RATE_LIMITED` analytics event for tracking server-side title generation limits.

eli5.text: Error messages that the assistant sends to its background monitoring tools now hide sensitive details like web addresses with tracking codes, login credentials, and the full text of your prompts. Additionally, the internal limit on how long an AI response can be has been refined so that it can only be lowered, never raised, ensuring that a user cannot accidentally exceed a safety cap set by the system. These adjustments happen silently in the background and do not change how you use the free coding tool day-to-day.
